approval_note: The committee cannot approve. PASS means no auditor found anything to veto on its own axis with the evidence it was given. Reading that as approval is a caller's policy -- pre-registration.md 6a -- and its error rate is unmeasured.

auditors.confidence_note: I verified the signal/feature ordering (_signal before _update, deques holding only prior closed bars), the coverage gate's use of only completed-session counters, and the absence of any scorer/dataset/split access; I could not see the harness's per-bar view implementation to independently confirm the structural guarantee.

The gate rejected the campaign outright (p=0.714, observed best -0.126 vs null max mean -0.112), so there is no positive claim to stress-test; the Sortino denominator (662 downside sessions of 960) is well-populated and the p-value is far above the resolution floor.

reasons: The economic evidence is internally inconsistent and cannot be reconciled with the strategy: net_pnl_points = -290,513.6 and gross_pnl_points = +127,665.8 imply commission_paid_points = 418,179.4, yet commission_per_contract_per_side_points is reported as 0.0, so the commission figure is not derivable from any stated rate and the cost share cannot be computed.

The magnitude is uninterpretable: 681 trades at 10 lots (0.001 BTC) on BTC perpetual cannot plausibly produce -290,513 index points of net P&L (roughly -$5.8M at $20/point) on that notional, and the evidence gives no per-trade return, notional, or price scale to reconcile it.

The stated metric is sortino_per_session with primary = -0.1261, but the strategy docstring's own arithmetic predicts a score near -0.134 at the 672-session floor and about -0.128 at 681 trades; the reported figure is better than the strategy's own bound, so the score cannot be tied to the P&L shown.

avg_holding_period_ns is 1.09e13 ns (~3.03 hours), which matches the 36-bar planned horizon but is inconsistent with the strategy's own claim that most trades hold 36 bars and only a handful are truncated at the session close; the evidence does not show the distribution needed to check this.

sessions_with_exposure (683) exceeds trade_count (681), which the strategy's own logic says is impossible (a session cannot be exposed without at least one fill), so at least one of the two counters is wrong.
auditors.confidence_note: No per-trade returns, notional, price scale, or commission rate are given, so I could not verify whether the negative net P&L is a real economic failure of the absorption-reversal claim or an artifact of the reporting; the code's direction (fade the absorbed flow) does match the pre-registered claim.

reasons: Breadth is narrow on every breakdown: only 11 of 32 months (34%), 2 of 7 weekdays (29%), and 8 of 24 hours (33%) are positive; the total is held up by a minority of periods.

Weekday distribution is severely lopsided: Wed (-140,390) and Tue (-93,418) alone account for the bulk of losses while only Thu (+13,145) and Sat (+7,196) are meaningfully positive, indicating the result is regime/weekday-specific rather than broad-based.

Monthly P&L is dominated by a handful of large winners (2024-03 +34,831; 2024-11 +29,293; 2024-12 +20,776) against many large losers (2025-07 -50,130; 2025-08 -97,791; 2025-04 -43,638), so the sign of the total depends on a few months.

Hour-of-day P&L is highly uneven (e.g. 03: +57,630 vs 05: -74,284 and 02: -71,393), and the entry-hour view disagrees sharply (02: -115,337; 03: -122,632), suggesting the realised-P&L view is driven by settlement timing rather than a stable intraday edge.
auditors.confidence_note: No out-of-sample validation was run, so I cannot assess whether this narrow distribution persists beyond the training sample; the veto rests on the in-sample breadth/concentration pattern alone.
